title: Drugs, Money & Miranda Rights: Tossed Drugs Goes Wrong!
description:
On September 29th, 2022, at 6:26 pm, a Circleville Police Department officer was on patrol, in his marked patrol vehicle, when he saw a gold Hyundai minivan. The officer saw the driver of the minivan fail to stop at a marked stop bar when he noticed a male passenger in the minivan who he knew had felony warrants. The male passenger exited the minivan and fled on foot from the officer who began his pursuit of the suspect. 

Another officer first noticed the gold Hyundai minivan with no other cars parked in the side lot of an Autozone. A white Toyota corolla pulled up beside the minivan driver’s window, the officer in his report stated “the two vehicles had not met for more than one minute, which based off my training and experience, is indicative of narcotics trafficking.” The officer followed both vehicles before losing visual and informing other officers of both vehicle descriptions. 

The primary officer began his pursuit of the male suspect and “unholstered his handgun” and ordered the suspect back in the vehicle. The suspect continued to run with, what the officer stated was “a clear bag” in his left hand. The officer continued to lawfully command the suspect to “stop running” before “holstering his handgun and unholstering his taser”. During the pursuit the officer witnessed the suspect throw the clear bag under a truck in another residence before surrendering at the other side of the truck. The officer who earlier witnessed the minivan, at the Autozone, then arrived on the scene to assist the primary officer in detaining the suspect.

The officers detained and handcuffed the suspect and advised him of his Miranda Rights. He admitted to the officer he knew he had a felony warrant and decided to run upon seeing the officer. The primary officer picked up the clear plastic bag containing “a large amount of rock-like substance and a white powder substance”. The suspect later went on to say to the officers he rode with the driver of the minivan to the Autozone to meet with a man in a white vehicle. He stated he saw the driver count “at least 300 dollars in cash” before reaching into the passenger window of the white vehicle and “exchanging the cash for narcotics”. The minivan driver then gave the male suspect said narcotics “to flee” from the officer.

Once meeting with the driver of the minivan who was asked to exit the vehicle, officers began questioning her on the bag retrieved earlier. The primary officer asked the driver to hand over her handbag where he counted approximately $62 inside. The primary officer then deployed his K9 to do a “free air sniff” of the gold minivan. The K9 did not indicate anything in the vehicle and upon further search of the vehicle nothing else was found. The driver was then placed under arrest, and advised of her Miranda Rights, before being placed into a patrol vehicle. 

Upon returning to the station the officers weighed and tested the substance found in the plastic bag at the scene. The results showed that the bag contained 29.09g Methamphetamine and inside a smaller bag 2.19g Fentanyl. Both substances along with the detained female’s dashcam and cell phone were secured as evidence. She was later charged with 3rd Degree Felony of Drug Possession Offenses, 3rd Degree Felony Tampering with Evidence, 3rd Degree Felony Drug Paraphernalia and 4th Degree Misdemeanor K9 Deployment.
